title.narrative: Child Project of the Global Clean Hydrogen Programme of Namibia

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The Namibia Child Project of the GCHP aims to contribute to the overall goal and impact of the programme along with the rest of the national child projects, working in a coordinated manner under the guidance of the Global Child Project. The activities envisaged for the Namibia Child Project will support the country’s energy transition by promoting the adoption of clean hydrogen technologies while delivering wide-ranging socio-economic benefits across the target sectors. The socio-economic benefits of the Namibia Child Project include: Capacity Building and Job Creation: By conducting capacity-building activities and awareness-raising through national events and workshops, as well as participation in thematic working groups, e-training sessions, and the Global Knowledge Platform managed by the Global Child Project, stakeholders will enhance their technical skills and expertise required for the development of the clean hydrogen market. These capacity-building efforts will directly contribute to the creation of skilled jobs and improve the quality of technical services offered by professionals in sectors linked to hydrogen production, infrastructure development, and technology management. The dissemination of knowledge and best practices will support local industries in developing a workforce capable of sustaining long-term growth in Namibia’s clean hydrogen economy. Innovation and Industrial Development: The Namibia Child Project will promote technological innovation by fostering collaboration among industry stakeholders, international experts, and local governments through support for strategic planning on green hydrogen implementation within industrial clusters and companies. By participating in the Global Knowledge Platform managed by the Global Child Project, Namibia will share best practices, innovation case studies, and local-level experiences, contributing to South-South cooperation and knowledge exchange. This will spur the development of hydrogen-related technologies and industries, opening new economic opportunities in sectors like energy, industry, and transport. The development of these industries will create direct and indirect jobs, strengthening Namibia’s position as a key player in the global green hydrogen economy. Energy Security and Economic Resilience: Through its focus on clean hydrogen, the Namibia Child Project will enhance energy security by supporting the production of locally sourced hydrogen as a reliable alternative to fossil fuels. This transition will reduce dependency on carbon-intensive energy sources, decrease the country’s carbon emissions, and diversify job opportunities. By strengthening national energy systems and supporting localised hydrogen production, the project will make Namibia’s economy more resilient to fluctuations in global energy markets, ensuring a sustainable and secure energy future. Gender Inclusion and Social Equity: The Namibia Child Project will actively promote gender inclusion by ensuring that women and youth participate in all project activities. The project aims for 50% female participation and 20% youth participation in relevant activities, creating opportunities for underrepresented groups in the clean hydrogen sector. Through the development of gender-responsive knowledge products and the inclusion of marginalised groups in capacity-building initiatives, the project will support social equity, providing equal access to employment opportunities and ensuring that the benefits of Namibia’s green hydrogen transition are widely shared across communities. Health and Environmental Benefits: By facilitating the adoption of clean hydrogen technologies, the Namibia Child Project will help reduce air pollution in industrial and urban areas, contributing to improved public health outcomes. Reducing reliance on fossil fuels will lower harmful emissions, improve air quality, and reduce health problems associated with pollution. Additionally, the project will contribute to significant reductions in greenhouse gas emissions, supporting Namibia’s climate change mitigation goals and fostering healthier environments for local communities. Knowledge Management and Sharing: The creation of the Global Knowledge Platform by the Global Child Project, coupled with the local development of knowledge products, will ensure continuous learning and access to the latest research, best practices, and technological advancements in clean hydrogen. This knowledge-sharing ecosystem will enhance Namibia’s capacity to innovate and implement clean hydrogen solutions, while building a global community of practitioners. The socio-economic benefits of this knowledge-sharing process will extend beyond the project’s lifespan, ensuring sustainable and enduring impacts at both national and international levels.

To enhance national institutional capacities, enabling policy frameworks, improve technological readiness and financial mechanisms for the successful uptake of clean hydrogen in Namibia to ensure its net zero development with social considerations and benefits.
